cards.text: Abram is ninety-nine years old now, and his son Ishmael, born to Hagar, is already part of the family (Genesis 16:15). Then the LORD appears to Abram. He says, “I am God Almighty. Walk before Me and be blameless.”

cards.question: God Almighty tells Abram He will establish something between Himself and Abram. What is it?

cards.text: Abram falls facedown, flat on the ground, and God keeps talking. When God Almighty introduces Himself, you do NOT answer with a little wave.

cards.question: God tells Abram what His covenant means for him. Abram will be the father of what?

cards.text: Then God changes his name: no more Abram, he's Abraham now. Meanwhile, the best name I ever got in the junk drawer was “why is THIS still in here?”

cards.question: God gives Abram the new name Abraham because Abram asked Him for a new one.

cards.text: God keeps going: He'll make Abraham exceedingly fruitful and make nations of him. Abraham walked in with ONE son, and God is talking NATIONS.

cards.question: Nations aren't all. God says ___ will descend from Abraham.

cards.text: And this covenant isn't only for Abraham. God says it's between Him, Abraham and Abraham's descendants after him, to be their God too.

cards.question: God makes His covenant with Abraham and his descendants. How long does God say it will last?
God promises Abraham and his descendants the land where Abraham is living now: all the land of ___.

cards.text: Now God tells Abraham his side of it. Abraham and his descendants after him must keep God's covenant.

cards.question: What does God say every male among Abraham and his descendants must do to keep the covenant?
God says circumcision will be a sign of the covenant between Him and Abraham.
Generation after generation, every baby boy among Abraham's people must be circumcised when he is ___ days old.
Only Abraham's own children and grandchildren must be circumcised.

cards.text: God makes it plain this is serious. A male who isn't circumcised has broken God's covenant.

cards.question: What does God say will happen to a male among Abraham's people who isn't circumcised?

answers.text: He will be cut off from his people
He will have to pay a fine
He will have to leave the land

cards.text: Now God turns to Abraham's wife, Sarai, and she gets a new name too: Sarah. Two new names in ONE conversation, friend, that's a whole family rebrand.

cards.question: God says He will bless Sarah. What will He surely give Abraham by her?
God says Sarah will be the mother of nations.

cards.text: Abraham falls facedown again. And then, right there on the ground, he laughs and says something to himself.

cards.question: As Abraham laughs, what does he ask himself?

answers.text: If a man of a hundred can have a child
Why God waited so long to speak to him
Whether Ishmael will become a great king

cards.question: Abraham also asks himself if Sarah can give birth at the age of ___.

cards.text: Then Abraham speaks up to God for someone close to him.

cards.question: Abraham tells God he wishes that ___ might live under His blessing.

cards.text: But God replies that Sarah will indeed bear Abraham a son. And God is NOT taking name suggestions, friend, He already picked one.

cards.question: What does God tell Abraham to name the son Sarah will bear?

cards.text: Then God says, “As for Ishmael, I have heard you,” and He promises to surely bless him. After years in the back of a drawer, I can tell you, “I have heard you” hits DIFFERENT.

cards.question: God promises to bless Ishmael and multiply him greatly. What will God make Ishmael into?
God says Ishmael will become the father of ___ rulers.
God says He will establish His covenant with Ishmael instead of Isaac.
God tells Abraham when Sarah will bear Isaac. When is it?

cards.text: When God finishes speaking with Abraham, He goes up from him. Now it's Abraham's move.

cards.question: God told Abraham to circumcise every male in his household. When does Abraham do it?

cards.text: THAT VERY DAY, just as God told him, and Abraham himself is circumcised at ninety-nine. I've watched people hit snooze NINE times on a Monday, and Abraham doesn't hit it once.

cards.question: Abraham's son Ishmael is ___ years old when he is circumcised.

cards.text: Abraham, Ishmael and every man of the household, those born there and those bought from foreigners, are circumcised on the same day. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this story has a whole lot more baking to do.

findings.problem: Hagar is named for the first time ('born to Hagar') without saying who she is. She is Sarai's Egyptian maidservant (Genesis 16:1).

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Genesis 17:5 gives the reason for the new name: 'for I have made you a father of many nations.' The card asks about a made-up reason (Abram asked for it), and no card ever tells the real one. The baker leaves without the link between the name Abraham and the promise, which is the point of the verse.

rule.text: Ask about the moments that move the passage forward and the details the baker needs to understand it.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'He will have to leave the land' is close enough to 'cut off from his people' that a baker could argue being cut off means being sent away. Replace it with an answer that is clearly different.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The joke 'God is NOT taking name suggestions' makes God the subject of the punchline and paints Him as brushing someone off. It also doesn't fit the moment: no one suggested a name. Abraham asked a blessing for Ishmael (17:18).

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: The answers are not the same kind of thing. 'A great nation' is a people, while 'A mighty priest' and 'A famous prophet' are single persons. The question's setup, 'multiply him greatly,' also rules out the two single-person answers, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Many choice cards are pure discovery with no story-card context to reason from. These include the number fill-ins: eight (stop 1 card 15), ninety (stop 2 card 6), twelve (stop 2 card 13) and thirteen (stop 2 card 19). Others are kings (stop 1 card 8), Isaac (stop 2 card 10), 'at this time next year' (stop 2 card 15) and 'on that very day' (stop 2 card 17). In stop 2, about half the choice cards can only be gotten by luck. Cut some, or give the story cards enough context that a thoughtful baker can reason out the pick.

rule.text: Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
